meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Temsirolimus alone extended median overall survival to 10.9 months versus 7.3 months with interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer; rash, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia were more common with temsirolimus.
data.abstract_excerpt: Interferon alfa is widely used for metastatic renal-cell carcinoma but has limited efficacy and tolerability. Temsirolimus, a specific inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin kinase, may benefit patients with this disease.

extracted_findings.species: Human – phase III RCT (n=626, poor-prognosis RCC)
extracted_findings.effect: Temsirolimus improved overall survival vs interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic renal-cell carcinoma
